title: Equity method investment — Halden Corp.
instructions: On January 1, Year 1, Halden Corp. paid **$900,000** for 30% of Bryce Inc.'s voting stock and gained significant influence. Round to the nearest dollar.

exhibits.title: Acquisition data
exhibits.content:
Bryce's book value of net assets on January 1: **$2,500,000**.

Bryce's building was undervalued by **$200,000** (remaining life **20 years**, straight-line). Any other excess is goodwill.

exhibits.title: Bryce, Year 1
exhibits.content:
Net income: **$400,000**

Dividends declared and paid: **$100,000**

rows.label: Halden's share of Bryce's net income
Amortization of the excess fair value of the building
Equity in earnings of Bryce reported by Halden

parts.prompt: Record Halden's equity in Bryce's earnings for Year 1.
parts.explanation: The share of income, net of excess amortization, increases the investment.

parts.prompt: How should each investment be accounted for?

rows.label: 15% of a listed company, plus 2 of 7 board seats and key technology sharing
rows.explanation: Board representation and technology dependence indicate significant influence.

rows.label: 25% of a listed company; a single investor holds the other 75% and ignores the investor
60% of the voting stock of a private company
5% of a listed company with no other relationship
rows.explanation: Equity securities with readily determinable fair values are measured at FV-NI.
